items.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006
items.q: Trombone Shorty with the trombone and a little kid with the trumpet.

ctx.x: Yes. “Trombone Shorty.” Okay now the trombone was bigger than he was when he started playing and he was maybe about that tall but he was playing that horn and he was getting this big sound. I remember I used to sing with the St. Louis Cathedral Choir. And we’d do a ten o’clock mass at the Cathedral. And one Sunday I came out of mass and I

heard this music but I didn’t see these people. And I went to the corner and it’s all these little boys, little boys. Trombone Shorty with the trombone and a little kid with the trumpet. And I imagine they were like nine, ten years old. There was a whole band of these kids. I got so excited I ran inside to the rectory and I said, “You guys got to come out here and see this.” And I think that the older gentlemen, the older players, just sort of took them in hand and said okay learn these songs, learn these songs.…
This group I mentioned started playing “Stand By Me,” you know? And what they did with it was indescribable. But it was so great, and they just went on forever — the endurance even, wow.
